messages:
emily_support: Heads-up — customer @janet reported an incident: intermittent 429s followed by duplicate side-effects (they're seeing two identical write operations). Happening only for a specific batch job using our Python SDK.
mike_support: Sorry to hear that. Do we have SDK version, exact error trace, and sample request? Any idempotency keys used?
emily_support: She sent logs and a small snippet. SDK pinned to 0.9.2 in their requirements.txt. Logs show sequences like: 503 -> retry -> 429 -> retry -> success, but the backend processed two writes. Attached paste of stack/logs below.
emily_support: ```
# simplified log excerpt
2026-02-28T14:03:21Z INFO request id=abc123 status=503
2026-02-28T14:03:21Z DEBUG retry backoff=0.45s jitter=0.0 seed=42
2026-02-28T14:03:21Z INFO request id=abc123 status=429
2026-02-28T14:03:21Z DEBUG retry backoff=0.30s jitter=0.0 seed=42
2026-02-28T14:03:22Z INFO request id=abc123 status=200
``` 
emily_support: They also send client code: ```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=..., session=None)
for item in items:
    resp = client.write(item, idempotency_key="op-123")
``` 
mike_support: Hmm idempotency_key is constant — that can explain duplicates only if server resets between retries. But the logs show the same request id and same seed for jitter (seed=42), and jitter=0.0 — odd.
anna_eng: @emily_support can you confirm whether they're using our default retry strategy or they overrode it? 0.9.2 had a bug where retry state could be shared across concurrent request objects when session was reused.
emily_support: They said they reused a single client across threads and didn't set any retry overrides; they rely on defaults.
anna_eng: OK that matches. In 0.9.2 there was a race where the internal backoff object got mutated across requests when the async session reused connection pools — causing non-monotonic backoff and sometimes skipping idempotency header re-attach on retry. That can lead to a retry being sent without the idempotency header or with stale token.
dmitri_eng: Repro steps I used in local: spawn 8 threads sharing a single client, force transient 503 then 429 from a mock server, and you'll see some retries drop the Idempotency-Key header. Here's the repro script I used:

dmitri_eng: ```python
# repro.py (uses httpx test server)
from redwood import RedwoodClient
import threading

client = RedwoodClient(api_key="x", _enable_retry_pooling=True)

def worker(i):
    # server flips 503->429->200
    client.write({"i": i}, idempotency_key=f"key-{i}")

threads = [threading.Thread(target=worker, args=(i,)) for i in range(16)]
for t in threads:
    t.start()
for t in threads:
    t.join()
```

dmitri_eng: On network capture you can see some retries missing the header.
emily_support: Customer is hitting this in prod intermittently during their nightly batch.
mike_support: Any suggested immediate workaround we can pass to the customer?
anna_eng: Short-term: either (1) upgrade to 0.9.7 which contains the backoff/headers fix; or (2) allocate a new client per request (not ideal) or set explicit idempotency per call and verify server-side rejects duplicates. Also ensure not reusing a custom session object into the client.
dmitri_eng: Also temporary workaround: set environment var RW_DISABLE_RETRY_POOLING=1 which forces per-request retry state until they can upgrade. We'll document that in a KB.
emily_support: I'll relay upgrade path and env workaround to Janet. Do we have a release note/bump we can link?
anna_eng: Release 0.9.7 notes: "fix: isolate retry/backoff state when using shared sessions; preserve Idempotency-Key on all retries; deterministic jitter seeding removed." Link: https://internal/releases/0.9.7 (internal)
dmitri_eng: Created internal ticket INF-2145 to backport to 0.9.6 patch branch for customers that can't upgrade to 0.9.7 ASAP.
mike_support: Thanks — can someone post a small blurb I can paste into the support reply summarizing cause + workaround?
anna_eng: Pasteable blurb: "Cause: older Python SDK versions (<=0.9.2) may, under high concurrency with a shared session, reuse internal retry/backoff state which can cause the Idempotency-Key header to be omitted on some retries. This can result in duplicate server-side writes. Workaround: upgrade to 0.9.7 (recommended) or set RW_DISABLE_RETRY_POOLING=1 or create a fresh client per request. We're also preparing a patch for customers who can't immediately upgrade (ticket INF-2145)."
mike_support: Perfect, I'll send that now. :thumbsup:
emily_support: Customer replied — they're going to try upgrading tomorrow during a maintenance window. I'll keep thread updated. :eyes:
deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: infra/0.9.7-hotfix -> staging at 2026-03-01T02:10:00Z
anna_eng: Follow-up: we should add a brief KB and a quickcheck script to detect header drops in customer environments.
emily_support: Agreed, adding to support playbook. Closing for now but will reopen if customer still sees duplicates after upgrade.
